'''Larry Donnell Nance Jr.''' (born January 1, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Indiana Pacers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Considered by many as one of the best big men ever to play in the [[Mountain West Conference]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wyoming Cowboys men's basketball|Wyoming Cowboys]] before being drafted 27th overall in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref name=bio>{{cite web|title=Larry Nance Jr. Bio|url=http://www.gowyo.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/larry_nance_jr_765297.html|website=GoWyo.com|access-date=March 17, 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150316203630/http://www.gowyo.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/larry_nance_jr_765297.html|archive-date=March 16, 2015}}</ref> Nance has also played for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[New Orleans Pelicans]], and [[Atlanta Hawks]].

==High school and college career==
Nance attended [[Revere High School (Ohio)|Revere High School]] near Akron, Ohio, growing to {{height|ft=6|in=7}} by his senior year after playing point guard for the freshman team standing at {{Height|ft=5|in=11}}. He averaged 18.2 points, 9.5 rebounds and 3.0 blocks per game as a senior for the Minutemen.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Pluto|first1=Terry|title=Larry Nance Jr. happy to continue his long, winding basketball road to Wyoming: Terry Pluto|url=http://www.cleveland.com/pluto/blog/index.ssf/2011/05/larry_nance_jr_happy_to_contin.html|access-date=June 26, 2015|agency=The Plain Dealer|issue=May 9, 2011|publisher=Plain Dealer Publishing Co.}}</ref>

In his four-year college career at [[Wyoming Cowboys basketball|Wyoming]], Nance averaged 11.3 points, 6.6 rebounds, 1.4 assists, 1.1 steals, and 1.1 blocks in 123 games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Larry Nance Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/larry-nance-2.html|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=June 26, 2015}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Los Angeles Lakers (2015–2018)===

==== 2015–16 season ====
On June 25, 2015, Nance was selected with the 27th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/150625_nancedraft | title=Lakers Select Larry Nance in First Round | work=NBA.com | date=June 25, 2015 | access-date=June 27, 2015}}</ref> Shortly after the draft selection was announced, an old tweet from 2012 by Nance resurfaced, in which he referenced then-teammate [[Kobe Bryant]]'s infamous [[Kobe Bryant sexual assault case|2003 rape incident]]. Nance deleted the tweet shortly after, and Bryant spoke on the tweet, calling the controversy surrounding it "water under the bridge".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kobe Bryant forgives Larry Nance Jr. for 2012 tweet calling Bryant a rapist|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2015/06/kobe-bryant-larry-nance-jr-rapist-tweet-response|access-date=November 22, 2021|website=USA Today|date=June 28, 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Larry Nance Jr. was 'terrified' of Kobe Bryant's response to tweet|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/lakersnow/la-sp-ln-larry-nance-terrified-kobe-bryant-tweet-20150629-story.html|access-date=November 22, 2021|website=Los Angeles Lakers|date=June 29, 2015 }}</ref> On July 10, Nance signed his rookie scale contract with the Lakers.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/150710_nanceSigns | title=Lakers Sign Larry Nance, Jr. | work=NBA.com | date=July 10, 2015 | access-date=July 13, 2015}}</ref> He made his NBA debut on November 6 against the [[Brooklyn Nets]], recording six points and five rebounds in a 104–98 win.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151106/LALBKN/gameinfo.html|title=Bryant, Lakers beat winless Nets for 1st victory|work=NBA.com|date=November 6, 2015|access-date=November 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151109024333/http://www.nba.com/games/20151106/LALBKN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=November 9, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 7, he made his first start for the Lakers after replacing [[Julius Randle]] at the starting power forward spot against the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/n/nancela02/gamelog/2016/|title=Larry Nance Jr. 2015-16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 27, 2015}}</ref> On December 27, he recorded his first career double-double with a season-high 17 points and 11 rebounds in a 112–96 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151227/LALMEM/gameinfo.html|title=Conley, Green lead Grizzlies past Lakers, 112-96|work=NBA.com|date=December 27, 2015|access-date=December 27, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160102094716/http://www.nba.com/games/20151227/LALMEM/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 2, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 1, 2016, Nance logged a season-high 14 rebounds, along with eight points, in a 93–84 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers vs Los Angeles Lakers Jan 1, 2016 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021500494|access-date=November 22, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref> He matched this total during his next game, which was two days later on January 3, along with fifteen points and a steal in a 97–77 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Phoenix Suns vs Los Angeles Lakers Jan 3, 2016 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021500510|access-date=November 22, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref> On January 14, Nance grabbed a season-high six steals in a 116–98 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers vs Golden State Warriors Jan 14, 2016 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021500592|access-date=November 22, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref>

==== 2016–17 season ====
On October 26, 2016, Nance made his season debut for the Lakers, recording five points, five rebounds and two assists in a 120–114 win over the Houston Rockets.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Houston Rockets vs Los Angeles Lakers Oct 26, 2016 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021600013|access-date=November 23, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref> On November 1, he recorded a season-high six steals in a 108–115 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers vs Indiana Pacers Nov 1, 2016 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021600048|access-date=November 23, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref> On November 20, he scored a career-high 18 points in a 118–110 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899648|title=Jimmy Butler's 40 points boost Bulls past Lakers, 118-110|work=ESPN.com|date=November 20, 2016|access-date=November 20, 2016}}</ref> On December 25, Nance was ruled out for four weeks after suffering an injury to his left knee.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/161225-nance-jr-injury-update|title=Larry Nance Jr. Injury Update|work=NBA.com|date=December 25, 2016|access-date=December 26, 2016}}</ref> He returned to action on January 22, 2017, where he logged four points and a rebound in a 73–122 blowout loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers vs Dallas Mavericks Jan 22, 2017 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021600662|access-date=November 23, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref> Nance matched his career-high of 18 points on February 3, where he also grabbed 11 rebounds and four assists in a 107–113 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers vs Boston Celtics Feb 3, 2017 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021600751|access-date=November 23, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref> On April 2, he recorded a season-high 14 rebounds, along with 12 points and three steals, in a 108–103 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies vs Los Angeles Lakers Apr 2, 2017 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021601143|access-date=November 23, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref> On April 9, Nance logged a season-high six assists, along with ten points and ten rebounds, in a 110–109 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Minnesota Timberwolves vs Los Angeles Lakers Apr 9, 2017 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021601202|access-date=November 23, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref>

==== 2017–18 season ====
On October 19, 2017, Nance made his season debut for the Lakers, where he recorded a double-double of 14 points and 12 rebounds in a 92–108 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=LA Clippers vs Los Angeles Lakers Oct 19, 2017 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021700016|access-date=November 23, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref> On November 3, he was ruled out for four to six weeks after fracturing the second metacarpal on his left hand the previous night against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/171103-larry-nance-injury-report|title=Larry Nance Jr. Medical Update|work=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2017|access-date=November 3, 2017}}</ref> He missed 11 games as a result.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975048|title=Clippers hang on to beat Lakers 120-115 for 3rd win in row|work=ESPN.com|date=November 27, 2017|access-date=November 28, 2017}}</ref> Nance returned to action on November 27, where he logged nine points, eight rebounds and four steals in a 115–120 loss to the Clippers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers vs LA Clippers Nov 27, 2017 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021700297|access-date=November 23, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref> On November 29, he also dished out a season-high five assists in a 123–127 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Golden State Warriors vs Los Angeles Lakers Nov 29, 2017 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021700312|access-date=November 23, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref> On February 6, 2018, two days before he was traded, Nance played his last game as a Laker, where he recorded six points, ten rebounds and a steal in a 112–93 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Phoenix Suns vs Los Angeles Lakers Feb 6, 2018 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021700804|access-date=November 23, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref>

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2018–2021)===
[[File:Larry Nance Jr. (38817215320) (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|right|Nance in 2018]]
On February 8, 2018, Nance was traded, along with [[Jordan Clarkson]], to his  hometown team the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for [[Isaiah Thomas (basketball)|Isaiah Thomas]], [[Channing Frye]] and a 2018 first-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Acquire Jordan Clarkson and Larry Nance Jr. From Lakers|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/clarkson-lnance-trade-180208|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 8, 2018|date=February 8, 2018}}</ref> After playing his first two games as a Cavalier with No. 24, he switched to No. 22 permanently on February 22 after the NBA allowed him to wear his father's retired No. 22 jersey.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975615|title=Wizards hold off LeBron, new-look Cavaliers 110-103|work=ESPN.com|date=February 22, 2018|access-date=February 22, 2018}}</ref> On March 5, 2018, he posted career highs with 22 points and 15 rebounds in his first start for Cleveland, as the Cavaliers defeated the [[Detroit Pistons]] 112–90.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975696|title=LeBron, Nance power Cavaliers past Pistons 112-90|work=ESPN.com|date=March 5, 2018|access-date=March 5, 2018}}</ref> On March 13, 2018, in a 129–107 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]], Nance had only four points, ending his career-best string of seven consecutive double-digit scoring games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975760|title=James' triple-double leads Cavaliers past lowly Suns|work=ESPN.com|date=March 13, 2018|access-date=March 13, 2018}}</ref> Nance helped the Cavaliers reach the NBA Finals in [[2018 NBA Finals|2018]], where they lost 4–0 to the [[Golden State Warriors]].

On October 15, 2018, Nance signed a four-year, $44.8 million contract extension with the Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/lnance-extension-2018|title=Cavs and Larry Nance Jr. Sign Multi-Year Contract Extension|work=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2018|access-date=October 15, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Haynes|first=Chris|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/sources-larry-nance-jr-agrees-4-year-45-million-extension-cavs-210542404.html|title=Sources: Larry Nance Jr. agrees to 4-year, $44.8M extension with Cavaliers|work=Yahoo.com|date=October 15, 2018|access-date=October 15, 2018}}</ref> On December 18, 2018, he had 15 points, a career-high 16 rebounds, six assists and the first game-winning shot of his pro career to give the Cavaliers a 92–91 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071132|title=Nance's tip gives Cavs rare road win as Pacers' streak ends|work=ESPN.com|date=December 18, 2018|access-date=December 18, 2018}}</ref> On January 8, 2019, against the Pacers, he suffered a right knee [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]] sprain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/status-update-larry-nance-jr-190110|title=Larry Nance Jr. Status Update|work=NBA.com|date=January 10, 2019|access-date=January 10, 2019}}</ref> He subsequently missed eight games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071395|title=Winslow scores 27, leads Heat past Cavaliers 100-94|work=ESPN.com|date=January 25, 2019|access-date=January 25, 2019|quote=Forward Larry Nance Jr. returned after missing eight games with a sprained right knee and had six points in 21 minutes.}}</ref> On February 8, he recorded a career-high 19 rebounds in a 119–106 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071492|title=Portis scores 30 in debut as Wizards beat Cavs 119-106|work=ESPN.com|date=February 8, 2019|access-date=February 8, 2019}}</ref>

On February 12, 2020, Nance scored a career-high 23 points, alongside twelve rebounds, two assists, three steals and two blocks, in a 127–105 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=CAVALIERS END 12-GAME HOME SKID, BEAT HAWKS 127-105 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900807 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On February 26, he grabbed a season-high 15 rebounds, alongside 13 points and three assists, in a 108–94 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=JOEL EMBIID SPRAINS SHOULDER, SIXERS LOSE TO CAVS 108-94 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900865 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On March 4, Nance grabbed 15 rebounds, alongside 19 points, four assists and four steals, in a 112–106 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=TATUM SCORES 32, LEADS CELTICS PAST CAVALIERS 112-106 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900917 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> During the 2019–20 season, Nance averaged a career-high 10.1 points per game.

On January 7, 2021, Nance scored a season-high 18 points, alongside three rebounds, four assists and three steals, in a 94–90 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=DRUMMOND'S DOUBLE-DOUBLE LEADS CAVS PAST GRIZZLIES 94-90 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000119 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 31, he grabbed a season-high 16 rebounds, alongside two points and four assists, in a 109–104 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=T-WOLVES SNAP 3-GAME SLIDE WITH 109-104 WIN OVER CAVALIERS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000311 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On March 17, Nance scored 18 points, alongside ten rebounds, four assists and two steals in a 117–110 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=SEXTON, GARLAND SHINE AS CAVALIERS END SLIDE, BEAT CELTICS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000620 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

=== Portland Trail Blazers (2021–2022) ===
On August 28, 2021, Nance was acquired by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in a three-team sign-and-trade involving the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Acquire Forward Larry Nance Jr. in Three-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-acquire-forward-larry-nance-jr-three-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=August 28, 2021|access-date=August 28, 2021}}</ref> He made his Trail Blazers debut on October 20, recording two points, three rebounds and two assists in a 124–121 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BARNES HAS 36 AND THE KINGS SPOIL PORTLAND'S OPENER 124-121 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100013 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2022–2024)===
On February 8, 2022, Portland traded Nance, [[CJ McCollum]], and [[Tony Snell (basketball)|Tony Snell]] to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for [[Josh Hart]], [[Nickeil Alexander-Walker]], [[Tomáš Satoranský]], [[Didi Louzada]], a protected 2022 first-round draft pick, the better of New Orleans' and Portland's 2026 second-round draft picks and New Orleans' 2027 second-round draft pick.<ref>{{Cite press release|date=February 8, 2022|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-complete-trade-new-orleans|title=Trail Blazers Complete Trade With New Orleans|publisher=Portland Trail Blazers}}</ref> Three days later, Nance underwent arthroscopic right knee surgery.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Larry Nance Jr. Medical Update|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/larry-nance-jr-medical-update-2-11-22|access-date=February 11, 2022|website=New Orleans Pelicans}}</ref>

On October 1, 2022, Nance signed a two-year, $21.6 million contract extension with the Pelicans.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Pelicans, Larry Nance Jr. reach 2-year, $21.6M extension, agent says |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34702369/new-orleans-pelicans-larry-nance-jr-reach-2-year-216m-extension-agent-says |date=October 1, 2022 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2024–2025)===
On July 6, 2024, Nance, [[E. J. Liddell]], [[Dyson Daniels]], [[Cody Zeller]] (via sign-and-trade), a 2025 first-round pick (via Lakers), and a conditional 2027 first-round pick were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Dejounte Murray]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hawks Acquire Dyson Daniels, E.J. Liddell, Larry Nance Jr., Cody Zeller, and 2 Future First-Round Draft Picks|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-acquire-dyson-daniels-e-j-liddell-larry-nance-jr-cody-zeller-and-2-future-first-round-draft-picks|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 6, 2024}}</ref> In 24 appearances (3 starts) for Atlanta during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], he averaged 8.5 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 1.6 assists. On March 26, 2025, Nance was ruled out for the remainder of the season due to a lingering right [[medial condyle of femur|medial femoral condyle]] fracture.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Provide New Update On Injured Center Larry Nance Jr|url=https://www.si.com/nba/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-provide-new-update-on-injured-center-larry-nance-jr-01jqa7vrj29y|access-date=April 16, 2025|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Return to Cleveland (2025–2026)===
On July 6, 2025, Nance signed with the Cleveland Cavaliers on a minimum deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Larry Nance Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-lerry-nance-jr-250706|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2025|access-date=July 6, 2025}}</ref> Nance made 35 appearances (including three starts) for the Cavaliers during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 3.7 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 1.0 assist.

===Indiana Pacers (2026–present)===
On July 9, 2026, Nance signed a one-year, $3.88 million contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Transactions|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-transactions-nance-brown-potter|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2026|access-date=July 10, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Nance is the son of [[Larry Nance]], Sr., a former professional basketball player for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] and [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref name=bio /> Nance Sr. was a three-time [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]] and won the league's first [[Slam Dunk Contest]]. Nance Jr. was a participant in the [[2018 NBA All-Star Game#Slam Dunk contest|2018 Slam Dunk Contest]], coming in second. One of the younger Nance's dunks was a tribute to his father, as he wore a retro 1984 Phoenix Suns uniform and performed a cradle dunk as his father had done that year to win the inaugural dunk contest. Larry Sr. and Jr. later teamed up for an [[alley-oop]] dunk, with the elder Nance throwing the ball up to his son, who slammed it through the hoop.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2018/02/larry-nance-jr-sr-dad-slam-dunk-champ-contest-honor-videos-nba-all-star-weekend|title=Larry Nance Jr. found the best way to honor his 1984 Slam Dunk champ dad|date=February 18, 2018}}</ref>

At the age of 16, Nance Jr. was diagnosed with [[Crohn's disease]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Darby|first=Luke|url=https://www.gq.com/story/real-life-diet-larry-nance-jr|title=The Real-Life Diet of Larry Nance Jr., the NBA Player with Crohn's Disease|work=gq.com|date=October 26, 2017|access-date=February 8, 2018}}</ref>

Nance Jr.'s older sister, Casey, played basketball at [[Revere High School (Ohio)|Revere High School]] and for the NCAA Division I [[Dayton Flyers]] for four years.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dayton.com/sports/archdeacon-former-flyer-teammates-future-marriage/I2VSM5E5OVGXRIXDDMRPR5CZEM/|title=Archdeacon: Former UD teammates plan their marriage|last=Archdeacon|first=Tom|date=June 27, 2021}}</ref> Nance Jr.'s younger brother, [[Pete Nance|Pete]] also played basketball at [[Revere High School (Ohio)|Revere High School]],<ref>{{Cite Outside of the NBA, Nance supports the soccer club [[Leeds United F.C.]] and became part owner in 2023 as a member of the 49ers Enterprises, the investment arm of the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Coates | first=Tom | title=NBA star confirms he is 'part of the ownership group' taking over Leeds United as new era beckons | website=Yorkshire Post | date=2023-06-10 | url=https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/sport/football/nba-star-larry-nance-jr-confirms-he-is-part-of-the-ownership-group-taking-over-leeds-united-after-49ers-enterprises-reach-agreement-4177716 | access-date=2025-12-12}}</ref>
